limitations: Successful model operations are async stubs. One real Axios loopback connection-refused failure was observed, without invoking an inference server. Resource devices are test configuration, not measured hardware.
PostgreSQL/Redis and BullMQ storage are real. Redis outage and lost DB acknowledgement are injected callback failures, not network partitions or server crash durability tests.
Two service instances in one Node process exercise database locks; operating-system process termination and remote model completion are not measured.
Migration checks execute the two new migrations up/down in an isolated schema with a minimal trips table, not the full historical production migration chain.
No production P50/P95, GPU VRAM, CUDA utilization, or physical CPU/GPU isolation can be inferred from these results.

Owner process termination references are fixture evidence. The tests enforce the contract but do not physically stop a prior process or establish inference-server-side fencing; pre-dispatch database ownership recheck is best effort.
